findings.summary: The .NET Foundation is a 501(c)(6) organization founded by Microsoft in 2014 to improve open-source software development around the .NET Framework. It operates license-agnostically, allowing projects to choose any OSI-approved license, and uses GitHub to host managed projects. Membership is open to contributors, who can vote in board elections. As of 2026, it stewards 556 active projects, including core .NET, Entity Framework, MSBuild, and NuGet, with a board of directors elected by members.

mechanisms.title: Governance via member voting
mechanisms.explanation: Anyone who has contributed to .NET Foundation projects can apply for membership. Members vote in elections for the board of directors, which preserves the health of the organization.

mechanisms.title: Project stewardship and hosting
mechanisms.explanation: The foundation uses GitHub to host open-source projects it manages. Projects accepted by the foundation are free to choose any open-source license, and the foundation stewards an expanding collection of active projects.

unknowns: The specific criteria used to select projects for inclusion under the foundation's stewardship
